newsitem.title: singapore: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's 1330 GMT release of the U.S. October housing starts figures, dealers said on Tuesday.
The housing starts figure is forecast to be 1.390 million units compared with 1.366 million units reported in September.
Traders were also waiting for the outcome of the U.S Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) policy setting meeting in Washington today.
"Rates were steady to higher in the morning on some position adjustments," a local dealer said.

"All eyes are on tonight's (U.S. October) housing starts figures and the outcome of the FOMC meeting. But I don't think there will be much impact as the (housing starts) numbers have been built into the market and the FOMC meeting is unlikely to adjust interest rates," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, Wednesday/Thursday rose 1/8 point to 5-7/16 5-5/16 and week-fixed rose 1/16 point to 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent.
Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Monday's 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent.
Four-months was unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16, nine-months rose 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent.
